items.title: Show HN: Earshot – old smartphone can listen to smoke alarm, doorbell or dog
items.contentSnippet:
TLDR: I’m building Earshot - the sound detection app that can detect (ideally) any sound described by text.
The neural model under the hood is a CLAP-style model (CLIP for audio): basically during the training you force the model make inner text and audio representations to match. And then you can use such model as 0-shot audio classifier. For POC I used LAION’s clap-htsat model but it turned out to be quite "heavy" so I’ve trained a smaller one by myself.

items.title: Show HN: Nexus – open-source local-first message routing for agents
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN, I built Nexus because I was tired of having multiple agents that I had to address one by one. I built an underlying mechanism where I could message all of them and have them have the capability to message each other and listen to wake events. I also got tired of having to run cron when I think that agents should have the capability to be event-driven.

items.title: Show HN: Cedric, the AI teammates that works in Slack and joins meetings
items.contentSnippet:
We built Cedric so anyone within a team, technical or not, could automate repetitive work through conversation.
It works in Slack, Discord, Telegram, or your browser, connects to thousands of tools. It shares a team memory with access controls, and joins meetings from which it can trigger actions.
Looking forward to your feedback!
